SMTO-EXE-0229 — SMTO couldn't find this Docker Compose project's files

GUID: ad5d79f7-05f3-59cc-99b2-85fb4e2083aa
Slug: docker-compose-project-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The project folder or Compose files given for this request don't exist on the Gateway computer, or the same file was listed twice. Nothing was started or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell SMTO the project folder's full location on the Gateway computer, starting from the top folder, for example /home/alex/myproject. SMTO only accepts a full folder location that exists on that computer.
  2. Name the Compose file or files exactly as they appear in that folder, such as compose.yaml, and list each file only once. Each listed file must really exist there, and a file listed twice is refused.
  3. Check that you picked the Gateway for the computer where the project folder lives. SMTO checks files only on the selected Gateway and never searches for a different project.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the project's settings and lists its services.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the project folder location, to the person who manages that computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Compose resolution on the Gateway rejected the request because working_dir is not an existing absolute directory, or a listed project file is missing, not a regular file, or duplicates another after path resolution.

What this means

  • Compose resolution rejected a nonabsolute/nonexistent working directory, duplicate resolved project files or a project file that was not a regular existing file. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Compose resolution rejected a nonabsolute/nonexistent working directory, duplicate resolved project files or a project file that was not a regular existing file.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact target-local working_dir and resolved files, including duplicates and file types.

How to fix it

  • Pass an absolute, existing working_dir on the Gateway host and project files that exist as regular files (relative names resolve against working_dir), with no duplicates after resolution. SMTO never auto-discovers a project, so correct the explicit inputs.
  • Correct the explicit local project directory and file list; do not auto-discover another project.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended distinct existing project files resolve under an absolute existing directory.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
